_readme: The scene manifest. One record per section of the component tour. Design fields (id, act, where, setPiece, covers) are read by the set pieces; where a section sits on the scroll, and for how long, is score.json; content fields (kicker, title, body, tags, staged, log and the per-section extras under 'copy') are read by the captions. Rewriting copy never moves a scene. A section with copy.exhibit gets the generic department exhibit from this data alone: the building lights those seats and a card shows members, figures and events. Every figure is stamped with the date it was counted. Sections marked staged are labelled as illustrations on the page.

beats.title: Not like employees. Employees.
beats.body: Everyone hunts for the best way to work with agents. The answer is plainer. Every problem a company has with people maps onto agents, so a hundred years of management practice applies. Agents have memory and skills, cooperate, make mistakes and respond to incentives. Hold the standup. Run the kaizen.

interlude.line: Four bylaws. Everything else follows from them.

beats.title: Every agent is an employee.
beats.body: Stop orchestrating a swarm. Staff a company. Every agent has a title, a desk and a record, and the org chart is the registry of them. A good manager does not blame someone. What separates a company that grows is how it handles mistakes and what it learns.

copy.quoteSource: From Flume's charter: the pillar every name in the repo is held to.

you.label: You
you.line: The only human on the chart.

departments.name: FLUME
departments.line: Hires, onboards, seats and reviews the agents.
departments.detail: Hires directors, managers and project managers, then onboards, seats and reviews them. The org chart is its record. A review ends in one of three verdicts: in good standing, on notice, or unable to assess.

departments.name: KREBS
departments.line: Runs every ticket's lifecycle, from filed to closed, on any board.
departments.detail: One lifecycle for every ticket, identical on every board: five lanes and a few labels. Krebs is the only dispatcher, and it ticks every 10 minutes.

departments.name: BLOODBANK
departments.line: Every memo in the building travels on one bus.
departments.detail: Every service, agent and component announces what it did and listens for what it needs on one bus. CloudEvents over NATS, with a schema for every event type, so a new department plugs in without anyone else changing.

departments.name: CANDYSTORE
departments.line: Every event ever sent, kept and searchable.
departments.detail: A permanent copy of every bus event, stored in Postgres, with query and summary APIs. A later session can recover what an earlier one did.

departments.name: CANDYBAR
departments.line: One clock fires every recurring job.
departments.detail: Cron, rebuilt on the bus. One heartbeat ticks every minute and every scheduled job is a consumer of it. No crontab, no private timers.

departments.name: SKILLEX
departments.line: One catalog of skills, installed on every agent's desk.
departments.detail: Skills are declared once, composed by reference and exposed to each agent CLI. A new skill is one folder that every agent can see.

departments.name: GENESIS
departments.line: The agent clients talk to about their projects.
departments.detail: Clients reach it through a public web desk and talk to one agent about their own projects.

departments.name: MILKSHAKE
departments.line: Turns usage and cost events into client billing.
departments.detail: Bus consumers with a database of their own: usage and cost events in, client billing out.

departments.name: INTAKE
departments.line: Files transcribed voice notes as tasks or notes.
departments.detail: Takes each transcribed voice note and files it as a task or a note.

departments.name: CRANK
departments.line: Nudges idle agent panes to keep work moving while you are out.
departments.detail: One crank per live agent session, clocked by Candybar. It wakes the crank officer only when a pane needs a poke.

departments.name: INFRA-DOCTOR
departments.line: Probes the homelab and platform, and flags what is broken.
departments.detail: Runs synthetic probes against the homelab and the platform and flags what is broken.

departments.name: HOLOCENE
departments.line: Where you look. Who is working, what is stuck, what needs you.
departments.detail: The operator's web app showing agents, schedules and events in one place, plus Holocene Auto for the car and Agent Pad for talking to one agent.

beats.title: Built from scratch, on purpose.
beats.body: 80 of the 100 components in the registry are first-party, built to one strict set of rules: layered abstraction, one owner for every building block, extension over rewrites, reuse over copies. A new component plugs in instead of rewiring the rest.

beats.body: A project registry and bootstrapper. One command registers a project, binds its ticket board, installs its skills and hooks and makes the first commit, from a shared template. It keeps 55 projects consistent and audits them against parity rules.

beats.title: Krebs. One ticket lifecycle, on every board.
beats.body: Every board uses five lanes and a few labels. A ticket entering Todo is triaged. Krebs is the only thing that moves it to In Progress, two slots per project. When the work comes back, the project manager gives the verdict. The same rules on every board.

beats.title: Pilot. From a transcript to tickets.
beats.body: Pilot is the ticket command line: agents and people read and move tickets without knowing a board's id or its API. Its harvest reads a transcript, finds the action items, groups them by project and files them on each project's own board. It speaks Plane and Trello.

beats.kicker: The power company. Tokens in, work out.
beats.title: The Gateway. Every model, under one name.
beats.body: A provider-agnostic, multi-tenant LLM gateway with a role-based router. Employees ask for a role, never a model. The router paces each subscription against its usage windows and reset times. When a pool runs out, it moves to the next: subscriptions, then metered, then free, with free pools held to 90% of each daily cap.

copy.aside: Cache tokens from every provider are counted one way, in one ledger. A thread stays with its model while its cache pays off. When it moves, its whole history goes with it.
copy.cardNote: Three roles: orchestrator, subagent, fast. Seven rungs. Every tenant gets the same roles, and each person's own subscriptions are walled off and spent first.
copy.punch: Pool 01 runs dry. The work moves on.
copy.stamp: Counted 21 Nov 2026: 112 routes, and a free family of 43 models in 13 pools. 147,215 usage records in the 7 days to 21 Nov. The dry pool and the new pool are an illustration.

decisions.line: 01 resets soonest, so it spends first. Nothing expires unused.
01 is out until it resets. 02 is furthest ahead of schedule, so it takes the work. Metered starts only when every subscription is spent.
Every night a scout looks for one more free provider. When one qualifies, it signs up, tests it and deploys it.

beats.title: HeyMa. Transcription, translation and dictation.
beats.body: HeyMa is the voice system. Wax transcribes recordings and runs cleanup passes on them. Vinyl turns speech into text while you are still talking. Phonograph translates a meeting live. Shortwave carries your phone's dictation into a terminal pane.

beats.title: Your transcript is waiting when you leave the room.
beats.body: Recordings are backed up first and never deleted, then transcribed locally on a GPU and run through a chain of passes: classification, speaker labels, spelling fixes, a title, the projects it touches.

beats.title: No Zoom? No problem. Speakers still get labeled.
beats.body: Diarization splits the recording by speaker. Then voice-id fingerprints each voice, matches it against a registry of voices and renames Speaker 1 to a name. A voice it has never heard is registered, and you are told.

beats.title: It reads itself. Jev makes the calls.
beats.body: Jev is a small model service for typed yes-or-no judgments. Wax asks it which projects a transcript touches, what kind of document it is and whether a respelled word fits its context. Turn-enricher asks it about every finished agent turn.
